title: Scalar endomorphisms imply absolute simplicity for rational algebraic-group modules
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $H$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional rational $H$-representation [def-wf-algebraic-representations]. A rational subrepresentation is a $k$-linear subspace preserved after extension by the action of $H(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$; simple means that the only rational subrepresentations are $0$ and $V$. A rational equivariant endomorphism is a $k$-linear map $f:V\to V$ such that $1\otimes f$ commutes with every element of $H(A)$ acting on $A\otimes_kV$, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Assume that $V$ is simple and that every rational equivariant endomorphism of $V$ is $a\,\mathrm{id}_V$ for some $a\in k$. For every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], the rational representation $K\otimes_kV$ of $H_K=H\times_kK$ is simple: the only $K$-linear subspaces preserved after extension by $H_K(A)$ for every commutative $K$-algebra $A$ are $0$ and $K\otimes_kV$. No smoothness, connectedness, reductivity, splitness or separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90--91; equivariant endomorphisms are defined in Remark 4.18, printed p.90.

proof.text: Put $C=k[H]$ with its coalgebra maps from [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. By [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], the given rational action is a right coaction $\rho:V\to V\otimes_k C$, and rational equivariant linear maps are precisely comodule maps. The subspaces in the item are precisely subcomodules: a subcomodule is stable by the displayed point-action formula in the dictionary; conversely an everywhere-stable subspace inherits the restricted natural action (the inverse action also preserves it), and the dictionary applied to its inclusion gives the restricted coaction. Thus $V$ has no nonzero proper subcomodule.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90–91; algebra reduction made explicit using Chapter 9(d), pp.174–175, and the double-centralizer theorem displayed in Proposition 14.1, p.279.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-coalgebra-dual-action-detection] to $(C,V,\rho)$. Let $B\subseteq\operatorname{End}_k(V)$ be the image of the resulting unital algebra map $C^*\to\operatorname{End}_k(V)$, $f\mapsto T_f$. This is a unital $k$-subalgebra and acts faithfully by inclusion. A $B$-stable additive subgroup is a $k$-subspace because $B$ contains every scalar map. The cited detection of subcomodules and Step 1 make $V$ a simple left $B$-module. Every additive $B$-linear endomorphism is $k$-linear for the same reason, and the intertwiner clause makes it a comodule endomorphism. Step 1 and the hypothesis imply that $E=\operatorname{End}_B(V)$ consists exactly of scalar maps $a1_V$, $a\in k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90–91; algebra reduction made explicit using Chapter 9(d), pp.174–175, and the double-centralizer theorem displayed in Proposition 14.1, p.279.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free]. It is finite: the coordinates of finitely many generators of $V$ use only finitely many basis indices, and every basis vector must have its index among these. It is nonempty since $V\ne0$. The same basis generates $V$ under the left $E$-action, since $E$ contains all scalars. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-simple-double-centralizer] hold for the faithful simple $B$-module $V$, finite over $E$. Every $k$-linear endomorphism $q$ commutes with $E$, since its elements are scalars, and so is $E$-linear. The cited surjectivity yields $b\in B$ acting as $q$. Consequently $B=\operatorname{End}_k(V)$: in particular every matrix unit for this basis equals some $T_f$.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90–91; algebra reduction made explicit using Chapter 9(d), pp.174–175, and the double-centralizer theorem displayed in Proposition 14.1, p.279.

proof.text: Fix any field extension $K/k$ and put $V_K=K\otimes_k V$, $C_K=K\otimes_k C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $H_K$ is affine with coordinate algebra $C_K$ (using tensor symmetry). It is finite type over $K$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], applied to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Under the dictionary [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary], its scalar-extended action has coaction $\rho_K(a\otimes v)=\sum_i(a\otimes v_i)\otimes_K(1\otimes c_i)$ whenever $\rho(v)=\sum_i v_i\otimes c_i$. Indeed, the dictionary evaluates this expression at a $K$-algebra point $x:C_K\to R$ as $\sum_i v_i\otimes ax(1\otimes c_i)$, exactly the original point action extended to $R$. The original coaction identities give those for $\rho_K$ by the same generator formula. A rational subrepresentation $W\subseteq V_K$ is therefore a $C_K$-subcomodule by Step 1 over $K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90–91; algebra reduction made explicit using Chapter 9(d), pp.174–175, and the double-centralizer theorem displayed in Proposition 14.1, p.279.

proof.text: For each $f\in C^*$ let $f_K:C_K\to K$ be the $K$-linear functional $f_K(a\otimes c)=af(c)$, well-defined by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Applying [lem-sfb-coalgebra-dual-action-detection] over $K$, the subcomodule $W$ is stable under $T_{f_K}$. The formula in Step 4 gives $T_{f_K}(a\otimes v)=\sum_i a f(c_i)\otimes v_i=a\otimes T_f(v)$. Thus $W$ is stable under the scalar extensions of every matrix unit from Step 3.

source.place: Proposition 4.19(b), printed pp.90–91; algebra reduction made explicit using Chapter 9(d), pp.174–175, and the double-centralizer theorem displayed in Proposition 14.1, p.279.

proof.text: The vectors $1\otimes e_i$ form a $K$-basis of $V_K$: the inverse coordinate map sends $a\otimes v$ to $(a e_i^*(v))_i$, by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $W=0$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise choose $0\ne w=\sum_i a_i(1\otimes e_i)\in W$ and an index $j$ with $a_j\ne0$. For every $i$, the extended matrix unit $E_{ij}$ sends $w$ to $a_j(1\otimes e_i)$ in $W$. Multiplication by $a_j^{-1}$ puts every basis vector in $W$, hence $W=V_K$. Since $K$ was arbitrary, this is the requested absolute simplicity.
